topic.title: Visual Architecture Design and Efficient Representation Transfer
topic.overview: This cluster studies how neural architectures learn useful visual features under constraints on data, parameters, or computation. Topics include convolutions, parameter sharing, layerwise training, attention, and transfer across sensing modalities. A representative architecture ties groups of convolutional filters through translations, seeking stronger representations or lower memory use through additional structure.
topic.whyItMatters: Architectural assumptions determine which patterns a model learns efficiently and which variations it handles naturally. Comparing accuracy with resource requirements and transfer behavior helps reveal whether a design captures useful structure or mainly benefits from scale.
topic.evolution: The representatives move from multiresolution and unsupervised convolutional models to structured convolutions and general attention-based perception. Recent work questions shape sensitivity and adapts pretrained layers for data-limited edge sensing, illustrating continued interest in both representational limits and practical reuse.
openQuestions: Which architectural changes improve shape and compositional understanding under controlled data budgets?
How can transferred layers be selected when source and target sensors have very different statistics?
